# Dimension 3: Schema Complexity & Capabilities

What JSON Schema features Claude supports, known limitations, and how complexity affects
reliability.

## Supported Features

From official Anthropic documentation [1][2][41]:

| Feature | Supported | Notes |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Basic types (object, array, string, integer, number, boolean, null) | Yes | |
| `enum` | Yes | Primitives only (strings, numbers, bools, nulls) — no complex types [1] |
| `const` | Yes | |
| `anyOf` | Yes | |
| `allOf` | Yes | `allOf` with `$ref` NOT supported [1] |
| `$ref` / `$def` / `definitions` | Yes | Internal only — no external URLs [1] |
| `default` | Yes | All supported types |
| `required` | Yes | |
| `additionalProperties: false` | Required | Must be false for all objects in strict mode [1][2] |
| String formats | Yes | date-time, time, date, duration, email, hostname, uri, ipv4, ipv6, uuid [1] |
| Array `minItems` | Partial | Only values 0 and 1 [1] |
| Nested objects | Yes | |
| Arrays of objects | Yes | |
| `input_examples` | Yes | Not for server-side tools [4] |

## Not Supported

| Feature | Status | Impact |
|---------|--------|--------|
| Recursive schemas | Not supported [1] | Hard failure |
| Complex types in enums | Not supported [1] | 400 error |
| External `$ref` (URLs) | Not supported [1] | 400 error |
| `minimum` / `maximum` / `multipleOf` | Not supported in strict [1] | Silently stripped by SDK |
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | Not supported in strict [1] | Silently stripped by SDK |
| `pattern` (regex) | Not supported in strict [6] | 400 error: "string patterns are not supported" |
| Array constraints beyond minItems 0-1 | Not supported [1] | Silently stripped |
| `if` / `then` / `else` | Not mentioned | Likely unsupported |
| `unevaluatedProperties` | Not mentioned | Likely unsupported |

## SDK Schema Transformation

SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Ruby, PHP) silently transform schemas before sending to the
API [1]:

1. Remove unsupported constraints (minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength)
2. Update descriptions with constraint info (e.g., "Must be at least 100")
3. Add `additionalProperties: false` to all objects
4. Filter string formats to supported list

"This means Claude receives a simplified schema, but your code still enforces all
constraints through validation" [1].

## Complexity Limits

No explicit numeric maximums are published, but several boundaries are documented:

- "Schema is too complex for compilation" — 400 error when limits exceeded [1]
- "The compiled grammar is too large" — ~50+ properties, ~8KB schema size threshold [22]
- 500 Internal Server Error with complex nested array schemas + `strict: true` — 17-55
  second response time before crash [23]
- 180-second compilation timeout as final backstop [1]
- Each optional parameter roughly doubles grammar state space [1]
- Combined complexity limits apply across all strict schemas in a single request [1]

## Schema Design Impact on Reliability

Schema design choices have dramatic effects beyond complexity limits [25]:

| Design Choice | Impact |
|--------------|--------|
| Field naming: `final_choice` vs `answer` | Accuracy dropped 95% → 4.5% [25] |
| Missing reasoning fields | Accuracy dropped 92-94% → 33% [25] |
| 3-4+ nesting levels | Failure rate increases to 1-2% [28] |
| Enum capitalization | Not guaranteed ("High" vs "high") [6] |
| `input_examples` added | Accuracy improved 72% → 90% [8] |

## Cross-Framework Benchmark Data (JSONSchemaBench)

Coverage on complex real-world schemas (GitHub-Hard tier) [13]:

| Framework | Simple Schemas | Complex Schemas | Feature Support |
|-----------|---------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| Guidance | >86% | 41% | 13/45 |
| Llamacpp | >86% | 39% | 1/45 |
| XGrammar | >86% | 28% | 1/45 |
| OpenAI | >86% | 9% | — |
| Outlines | >86% | 3% | 0/45 |
| Gemini | >86% | 0% | — |

"No framework covers all 45 JSON Schema feature categories" [13]. Note: Claude/Anthropic
not included in this benchmark [13].

XGrammar exhibited 38 under-constrained failures — "corrupts data at runtime without any
signal" [13].

## Gaps and Limitations

- No published complexity thresholds (exact property count, nesting depth, or schema size limits)
- No Claude-specific benchmark in JSONSchemaBench
- SDK silent stripping of unsupported constraints creates a gap between what the developer
  specifies and what the model sees
- "format" keyword accepted as annotation but not enforced by SDK validator [3]
